verdict.summary: You can connect your own account in minutes while the app is in Testing mode. Opening it to the public with most useful Gmail scopes (readonly, modify, compose, and Composio's default full-access https://mail.google.com/) means restricted-scope verification, which Google estimates at about 6 weeks, plus a third-party CASA security assessment every year. If you only send mail with gmail.send, review drops to sensitive-scope verification, estimated at about 10 business days.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours for Testing mode; several days spread over the verification period (privacy policy, domain verification, demo video, scope justifications, CASA work)
verdict.approval_wait: Restricted scopes: about 6 weeks (Google's estimate, not guaranteed) plus the CASA assessment. Sensitive scopes only: about 10 business days. Brand verification: 2-3 business days.

gates.name: Testing mode (you as a test user)
gates.unlocks: You connect your own Gmail account through your own OAuth client, with any scopes, and no verification.
limits: You click through a tester warning screen
Refresh tokens expire after 7 days in Testing, so you have to reconnect weekly
Requires a Google account to sign in to Cloud Console

gates.name: Testing mode with listed test users (or unverified In production)
gates.unlocks: Invited test users, or a small number of early users, can connect before verification.
limits: Test users must be listed on the app and click through the tester warning screen
A user cap applies. Unverified apps that request sensitive or restricted scopes are limited to 100 new users
Refresh tokens expire after 7 days while the app is in Testing
An unverified app moved to In production shows the unverified-app screen, and the 100-user cap is lifted only by verification
Reported: 100 refresh tokens per Google Account per client ID. Creating a new one invalidates the oldest

gates.name: In production + verified (brand, sensitive/restricted scope verification, CASA)
gates.unlocks: Any Google user can connect with no warning screen and no user cap.
limits: Restricted-scope apps must be reverified and pass a security assessment at least every 12 months
CASA assessor fees are agreed directly with the assessor. Google charges nothing
The whole Cloud project is reviewed, so every OAuth client in it must be ready
gates.time_to_reach: Brand verification: 2-3 business days. Sensitive scopes: about 10 business days. Restricted scopes: about 6 weeks plus the CASA assessment

steps.title: Sign in to Google Cloud Console and create a project
steps.detail: Sign in with a Google account at console.cloud.google.com and create (or pick) a project used only for this app. Restricted-scope verification covers the whole project, so don't mix unrelated test clients into it.
gotchas: Separate test OAuth clients in the same project can block verification later.

steps.title: Enable the Gmail API in the project
steps.detail: In the project's API library, enable the Gmail API so that tokens can call it. Composio's default scopes also include People/contacts scopes. Enable that API too if you keep them.
gotchas: The research did not check the exact console labels for this step.

steps.title: Pick the smallest scope set
steps.detail: Map each agent feature to the narrowest Gmail scope. gmail.labels is non-sensitive. gmail.send is sensitive. gmail.readonly, compose, insert, modify, metadata, settings.* and https://mail.google.com/ are restricted. Drop https://mail.google.com/ from Composio's defaults unless you must permanently delete mail or use IMAP/SMTP.
gotchas: Copying Composio's default scope list brings in the restricted full-access scope and its full verification burden.

steps.title: Configure branding and declare scopes on the Data Access page
steps.detail: In Google Auth Platform, fill in Branding: app name, support email, home page and privacy policy links. Then list every scope you will request on the Data Access page, where Google groups them as sensitive or restricted.
gotchas: The research could not check the exact menu paths because Cloud Console was behind a login wall.

steps.title: Keep the app in Testing and add test users
steps.detail: Leave the publishing status as Testing and add your own Google account plus any invited testers as test users. Testers will see a warning screen, and their refresh tokens expire after 7 days.
gotchas: Weekly token expiry in Testing breaks long-running agent connections. Plan to reconnect.

steps.title: Create a Web application OAuth client
steps.detail: Under Credentials, create an OAuth client ID with Application type set to Web application. Add the Composio callback as an authorized redirect URI, then copy the client ID and client secret.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The redirect URI must exactly match oauth_redirect_uri on the Composio auth config (currently https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback).

steps.title: Create a Composio Gmail auth config with your credentials
steps.detail: In the Composio dashboard, create a Gmail OAuth2 auth config, turn on 'Use your own developer credentials', and enter the client ID, client secret, redirect URI and your trimmed scope list. You can also do this through Composio's API.

steps.title: Run a test authorization
steps.detail: Start a connection for your own account and confirm that the consent screen shows your app name and that tokens come back. Google's endpoint rejects unknown client IDs with invalid_client, which helps you spot a mis-pasted client ID.
gotchas: Google grants scopes only at consent time. After you change scopes, existing users must reconnect.

steps.title: Verify your domain and publish branding
steps.detail: Verify ownership of your home-page domain in Search Console. Host a privacy policy on the same domain that explains how you handle Google user data and meets the Limited Use requirements. Then run the branding check in Cloud Console and publish the result.
gotchas: A passing branding result expires if you don't publish it within 7 days.
Branding must be published before you can request data-access verification.

steps.title: Prepare scope justifications and a demo video
steps.detail: An agent can draft a written justification for each sensitive or restricted scope, explaining why narrower scopes won't work, and a script for the demo. You record an unlisted YouTube video showing the grant flow, the consent screen with the app name and client ID, and each scope in use.
gotchas: The video must show the client ID on the consent screen.

steps.title: Switch to In production and submit for verification
steps.detail: Set the publishing status to In production and submit the project for verification from Cloud Console. Make sure every OAuth client in the project is ready first.
gotchas: You can add new scopes during review, but users see the unverified screen and the 100-user cap until those scopes are approved.

steps.title: Wait for Google's review
steps.detail: Google estimates about 10 business days for sensitive scopes and about 6 weeks for restricted scopes, with no guarantee. Until approval, the 100-new-user cap and unverified screen still apply.

steps.title: Complete the CASA security assessment (restricted scopes)
steps.detail: If your servers store or transmit restricted Gmail data (as a Composio-brokered agent does), hire a CASA-authorized assessor. Your tier depends on data sensitivity, user counts and risk signals. Repeat the assessment and reverification every 12 months.
gotchas: The assessor's fee is agreed directly with the assessor. Google charges nothing.

requirements.item: Google account with access to Cloud Console
requirements.detail: Cloud Console is behind a Google sign-in wall.

requirements.item: Exact redirect URI match with the Composio auth config
requirements.detail: The redirect URI on the Google client must match oauth_redirect_uri in Composio exactly.

requirements.item: Public home page and privacy policy on a verified domain
requirements.detail: The privacy policy must be on the same domain as the home page, linked from the consent screen, disclose how Google user data is handled, and meet Limited Use. The domain must be verified in Search Console.
Branding must be published before data-access verification. Passing results expire after 7 days if not published.

requirements.item: All scopes declared on the Data Access page, with justifications
requirements.detail: Declare every scope and explain why narrower scopes won't work.
Must show the grant flow, the consent screen with the app name and client ID, and use of each sensitive or restricted scope.
Required for restricted scopes when the data is stored on or sent through servers. Done by an authorized assessor and repeated every 12 months.

scopes.effect: Full access, and part of Composio's defaults. Triggers restricted verification plus CASA. Google says to request it only for permanent deletion; IMAP/SMTP also need it.
Reading mail requires restricted verification and CASA.
Restricted verification even though it gives metadata only.
Sensitive-scope verification (about 10 business days), no CASA. Use it instead of the full scope for send-only apps.

blockers.symptom: Google shows that the app is blocked, or users see the unverified-app screen
blockers.cause: The client requests scopes that have not been verified.
blockers.fix: Remove the extra scopes, or declare them and submit them for verification.

blockers.symptom: Verification submission is held up even though your main client is ready
blockers.cause: Restricted-scope projects are reviewed as a whole, including every OAuth client in the project.
blockers.fix: Move test and dev clients to a separate project, or get them ready too.

blockers.symptom: An IMAP/SMTP-based integration is pushed into restricted-scope review
blockers.fix: Switch send-only flows to the Gmail API with gmail.send (sensitive), or accept restricted verification plus CASA.

blockers.symptom: Connections stop working after about a week
blockers.cause: Refresh tokens issued while the app is in Testing expire after 7 days.
blockers.fix: Move to In production. Note this brings the unverified screen and 100-user cap until you are verified.

blockers.symptom: redirect_uri_mismatch or a failed callback during connection
blockers.cause: The redirect URI registered with Google differs from the one on the Composio auth config.
blockers.fix: Paste the exact Composio callback URL into the Google client's authorized redirect URIs.

blockers.cause: An unverified app requests sensitive or restricted scopes.
blockers.fix: Finish verification. The cap is lifted only after successful verification.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed Gmail OAuth so you can build without Google review. Switch to your own Google OAuth app when you need your app name on the consent screen, custom scopes, or your own rate quota. If you copy Composio's defaults, you get the restricted https://mail.google.com/ scope, which means about 6 weeks of verification plus annual CASA. Trim the list first. The redirect URI on the Google client must exactly match the one on the Composio auth config.
